newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to decide in weeks on grain duties, PM says.
newsitem.headline: Poland to decide in weeks on grain duties, PM says.

text.p: Poland may consider in a few weeks' time whether to withdraw its temporary duty-free quota for grain imports, if studies show that it has enough grain, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Tuesday.

"If analysis of the grain market, especially of reserves, reveals that there is enough grain to last until the next harvests, then we can return in a few weeks time to the issue of removing the quota for duty free imports of grain," PAP news agency quoted him as saying before a cabinet meeting.
The 20 percent duty on grain imports, designed to protect domestic farmers, was suspended last year until June 1997 to curb inflation and rein in sharp growth in grain prices.

Last week Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski of the Polish Peasant Party (PSL) said he would propose at the cabinet meeting that the duty-free quota should be immediately withdrawn, as the grain market's situation was stable and forecasts for the next harvest were good.
